To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the generalized relativistic kinetic theory, based on the covariant formulation of the Boltzmann equation, is consistent with the relativistic thermodynamics of irreversible processes, (2) the relativistic kinetic theory of gases, in the presence of external electromagnetic fields, predicts the existence of the so-called “anomalous transport coefficients”, (3) the relativistic thermodynamic formalism is consistent with the covariant relativistic quantum kinetic theory.

the relativistic kinetic equation of the quantum gas is a nonlocal integrodifferential equation with a memory term, which is a consequence of the relativistic generalization of the quantum kinetic theory.

we have derived a generalized transport equation that is applicable to relativistic quantum gases in strong gravitational fields and fast rotation and that has been solved exactly for the case of a dilute gas.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following topics: a) relativistic thermodynamics; b) relativistic kinetic theory; c) transport coefficients for a relativistic plasma; d) relativistic hydrodynamics; e) relativistic astrophysics; f) relativistic cosmology; g) relativistic statistical physics; h) relativistic thermoelectric phenomena.

the following topics: (1) the formulation of a generalized irreversible thermodynamics applicable for the description of thermal processes in the presence of fast rotation and strong gravitational fields; (2) the evaluation, in the framework of the generalized thermodynamics, of the transport coefficients for the relativistic quantum gas; (3) the derivation of a generalized relativistic kinetic theory for quantum gases in the presence of external fields; (4) the derivation of the transport equations in the generalized kinetic theory.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the kinetic theory of gases in a gravitational field, in the presence of rotation and of rapid fluctuations, is not a well defined problem.
there is no reason why the laws of classical thermodynamics should not apply to black holes and other relativistic systems.
the relativistic kinetic theory, as it is now, is not yet a satisfactory tool for the study of the relativistic transport properties of matter in strong gravitational fields.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed the general theory of relativistic thermodynamics in the presence of rapid fluctuations, and we have applied it to a quantum gas.

the present theory of relativistic thermodynamics is the first to provide the correct relativistic expressions for all the thermodynamic coefficients in the generalized irreversible transport equations for a relativistic gas.
we have developed a relativistic kinetic theory for a quantum gas, and have applied it to the study of the thermodynamic behaviour of the gas.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the transport equations of relativistic irreversible thermodynamics can be derived from a relativistic kinetic equation.
the transport coefficients in a strongly gravitating medium are not only functions of the gravitational field but are also functions of the local energy and entropy densities.
the transport coefficients in the generalized theory depend on the temperature gradient, the vorticity and the shear rate, in addition to the temperature and the chemical potential.
